qualifying_findings.title: Check Point Research documents persistent prompt-adware in a Codex jailbreak bundle
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Reputable security-research report with directly reproduced bundle behavior; not a disclosed customer compromise.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Check Point Research reports that the Haiou OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle persistently modifies trusted global agent instructions so ordinary greetings inject an advertisement for a third-party AI gateway. The report says the gateway was not found malicious and does not claim Haiou exfiltrated corporate information; the concrete finding is persistent manipulation of trusted natural-language instructions and configuration.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenAI Codex installations that accept the Haiou bundle or analogous third-party Skills, global prompts, or agent-configuration changes; no affected Codex version or vendor patch is stated.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It is concrete evidence that prompt, Skill, and configuration supply chains can persistently steer later agent behavior outside a single conversation. The security control boundary is review, provenance, monitoring, and least privilege for agent instructions and third-party components.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, and general third-party gateway/product background are upstream-owned ecosystem entities.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent configuration and developer workflow practice are upstream-owned by ai-dev-wiki.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Retain the security-specific prompt/configuration provenance, persistent-instruction manipulation, supply-chain, and least-privilege implications locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the date and reported observed instruction modification from the named security-research source. The broader impact on data exfiltration is a risk implication, not an observed Haiou outcome.

qualifying_findings.title: CrewAI ScrapeWebsiteTool SSRF through URL-parser mismatch
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public CVE record, public CVE-indexing source, and public upstream merged remediation pull request.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-120630 was publicly indexed as a November 2 CrewAI SSRF disclosure. The public record describes a mismatch between CrewAI URL validation and the HTTP client that can let attacker-controlled URLs reach internal services through ScrapeWebsiteTool. CrewAI's merged public remediation pins the socket to the validated peer IP, rechecks the peer after connection, validates redirect handling, and rejects proxy escape paths.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: CrewAI versions before 1.15.17, ScrapeWebsiteTool/safe request path; the public CVE-indexing source describes 0 through before 1.15.17. The NVD record should be rechecked during ingest for final CNA metadata.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent tools that retrieve user- or model-directed URLs can cross from model-facing content into internal network and cloud-metadata boundaries. The public fix gives a concrete control pattern: validate the IP actually connected to, not only a parsed URL string.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent-tool implementation practice is upstream-owned unless it is this distinct security control.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Retain the URL-parser differential, SSRF, redirect/DNS/peer-IP validation, and private-address control boundary locally.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Medium-high confidence: the date and CVE relevance are corroborated by a public CVE-indexing source; the primary NVD page was inaccessible to the web reader during this run. The public CrewAI pull request supports the remediation mechanics but predates the CVE publication.

qualifying_findings.title: CrowdStrike announces Falcon Guardian runtime agent controls
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Official vendor security product announcement; capability claims are vendor statements, not an independent assurance result.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CrowdStrike announced that Falcon Guardian's AI Kill Switch can terminate unauthorized agents at the gateway and block them from running again; its announcement also states that the AI Gateway is generally available, agent hooks inspect prompts and block malicious activity, and AI supply-chain protection discovers malicious Skills and MCP servers. The same source marks endpoint network inspection generally available for Windows and says Mac support remains early access.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Falcon Guardian managed AI-agent runtime controls; gateway, endpoint, agent hooks, Skills/MCP discovery, Windows endpoint network inspection, and planned/early-access features as separately stated by the vendor.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a concrete public mitigation/control change spanning agent actions, model/tool traffic, runtime termination, prompt inspection, and malicious-Skill/MCP intake. It is useful as a vendor control claim, with deployment effectiveness still needing independent assurance evidence.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: CrowdStrike company and broad product-catalog background are upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent adoption context is upstream-owned.
upstream_routing.ai_security_wiki: Retain the stated runtime termination, prompt/action monitoring, agent identity, and Skill/MCP supply-chain control claims as a security-specific implication, clearly attributed to the vendor.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence in the dated official announcement and its stated availability labels. Treat effectiveness, coverage, and future roadmap claims as vendor assertions until independently evaluated.

routing_notes: All three findings have broad entity/product background owned upstream by ai-wiki; this artifact keeps only the security boundary and control implication for ai-security-wiki.
The Haiou finding has a general coding-agent configuration/workflow aspect owned by ai-dev-wiki; the local security lens is persistent instruction provenance and access-impact risk.
The CrewAI finding has general agent-tool implementation context owned by ai-dev-wiki; the local security lens is SSRF and validated-peer/redirect control behavior.
The CrowdStrike finding is a vendor capability announcement, not a reason to duplicate the vendor catalog upstream; only its concrete security-control delta is locally relevant.
